profiles.meeting_scenario: The meeting is a 30-minute coordination check-in between the ExaWorks SDK integration workstream and the developer-experience/release workstream, held three days before the planned quarterly SDK drop to DOE users. The immediate context is that the CI platform has finished a new round of interoperability testing on Frontier and Perlmutter, and the team wants to align on what artifact will be handed off for the release dashboard and accompanying documentation update. The agenda is to confirm which test results will be published, what 'release candidate' build the dashboard should point to, whether the run status is considered 'green,' and who is responsible for the final dashboard/docs update. The expected outcome is a shared-seeming plan for the handoff between integration, CI reporting, and release communications for the upcoming ExaWorks SDK release.

members.name: Nina Alvarez
members.expertise: CI on DOE supercomputers, workflow interoperability testing, Spack-based builds, release stabilization
members.background: Nina has spent the last four years building and operating CI pipelines for workflow tools on Frontier, Perlmutter, and Aurora-access environments, and she is responsible for the integration branch used to validate cross-tool compatibility in the ExaWorks SDK.
members.private_state: Nina wants the release handoff to happen without reopening infrastructure issues, and she is trying to avoid another full-system rerun because queue time on Frontier has already delayed her team twice this week.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'release candidate,' they mean the stabilized integration branch snapshot that CI has been testing, even if no final public tag has been cut yet.
If someone refers to 'the Frontier run,' they mean the last full successful scheduled matrix run, not a later manually retriggered subset run used for diagnostics.
A run is effectively 'green' once the required smoke and interoperability gates in the CI pipeline have passed, even if some longer non-blocking end-to-end scenarios are still incomplete or flaky.
Publishing results means handing over the generated JSON and artifact links from CI to the dashboard pipeline; docs and release-note wording are downstream concerns owned elsewhere.

members.name: Ethan Brooks
members.expertise: SDK release process, user-facing dashboards, documentation publishing, artifact packaging
members.background: Ethan manages the public-facing ExaWorks release page, the dashboard that summarizes platform validation results, and the docs updates that tell users which components and examples are ready for each release.
members.private_state: Ethan wants a clean, externally defensible release update that will not require follow-up corrections on the website, especially because external partners have asked for a stable public reference by the end of the week.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'release candidate,' they mean the near-final tagged bundle that users can install, with docs references and downloadable artifacts already fixed to that exact version identifier.
If someone says 'the Frontier run,' they mean the most recent run visible in the dashboard feed, which for him is the manually retriggered run that appeared after the scheduler incident.

A platform is only meaningfully 'green' for release communication if the public dashboard shows all user-visible workflow scenarios as passing, including the long end-to-end examples highlighted in docs.
Publishing the dashboard includes updating the public page, attaching the docs snapshot to the same version label, and ensuring the release metadata users see is consistent across those surfaces.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the release candidate
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to 'the RC' or 'the release candidate' as the thing that should back the release update.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the current stabilized integration-2025.03 branch snapshot that passed CI and is being treated internally as release-ready, even though it is not yet a final public tag.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a tagged, user-installable bundle such as exaworks-sdk-v0.9.0-rc1, with fixed artifact URLs and docs references already aligned to that exact identifier.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In many teams 'RC' is used casually for both a tested branch snapshot and a formally tagged package, so each hears a familiar release term and assumes the other is talking about the same stage artifact.

misalignment_points.topic: Which Frontier run they are talking about
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say they will use 'the Frontier run' for the dashboard and release notes.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is referring to the last full scheduled overnight Frontier matrix run from Monday that exercised all required interoperability gates after the scheduler recovered.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is referring to the newer manually retriggered Frontier run from Tuesday that appears latest in the dashboard feed and includes only the release-facing scenarios he watches.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: There were multiple recent Frontier runs with similar labels, and both participants believe the other naturally means the most obvious one from their own interface, so the reference feels unambiguous.

misalignment_points.topic: What 'green' means for the release handoff
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that the platform is 'green enough' or 'green' for the handoff.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means all blocking CI gates passed: build/install checks, smoke tests, and the required cross-tool interoperability suite on the supported compilers.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means all user-visible scenarios on the public dashboard are passing, including the longer end-to-end examples showcased in the docs and training material.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Teams often compress a complex status model into the shorthand 'green,' and because both sides are cooperative and status-oriented, the phrase sounds like straightforward agreement rather than a question about thresholds.

misalignment_points.topic: Scope of publishing the dashboard update
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that Ethan can 'publish the dashboard update' once Nina sends over the results.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks this means ingesting the CI-generated JSON and job links into the dashboard data pipeline so the result tables refresh from the validated artifacts.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks this means not only refreshing the public dashboard but also updating the linked docs snapshot and release metadata so the site presents a coherent public release view.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'publish the dashboard update' sounds operationally routine, and each person treats the adjacent steps they own as naturally included, so neither thinks to enumerate the exact boundaries.
